I've been farming this land since I was young, watching my father and learning from the neighbors. I don't read much, but I know this soil and I know what works in Quzhou. The North China Plain — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's what my father did, that's what I do. No reason to change what feeds the family and pays the bills.

My land is about 12 mu. All of it goes into the wheat-corn rotation. I planted the winter wheat back in October already — it's coming up now. Come June when the wheat is cut, I'll put corn in right away. Can't waste a day.

For wheat, I use the Jimai variety everyone around here uses. Improved seed, yes — I stopped saving my own seed years ago when the yields dropped. I put down urea and compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress at jointing. My neighbor says I use too much fertilizer but I haven't had a bad harvest. I irrigate — at least three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. Maybe a fourth if it's dry at grain fill. I'll spray once or twice for aphids and rust, and maybe a herbicide early on.

For corn, I buy Xianyu 335 from the village supply store. Hybrid, same as everyone. I plant it no-till right into the wheat stubble to save time and water. I pour on nitrogen — one big application plus a top-dress. One or two irrigations if rain is short. Spray for stem borer if needed.

I'm 61 and my knees aren't what they were. I pay someone with a rotary tiller to prepare the wheat seedbed. For corn I go no-till to save the trouble.
